characters.name: As a Whole
characters.description: The Beautiful Elite: Nearly all of the main cast is great-looking, their characters seem to have an infinite amount of money and accessories (depending on what the plot needs) and are apparently just great at everything they do. Given brilliantLampshadingby Sinjin inThe Slap Fight. Beauty, Brains, and Brawn:Cat is the Beauty, Tori is the Brains, and Jade is the Brawn.Also for the guys: Beck is the Beauty, Robbie is the Brains, and Andre is the Brawn. Cat is the Beauty, Tori is the Brains, and Jade is the Brawn. Also for the guys: Beck is the Beauty, Robbie is the Brains, and Andre is the Brawn. Everyone Has a Special Move: Despite them taking a variety of subjects at Hollywood Arts and everybody can seem likeThe Aceat everything, there's one special skill that seems to be their focus and what drives a lot of their storylines: with Tori it's singing, Beck - acting, Jade - writing & directing, Andre - song writing and composing, Robbie seems like the most tech-adept of the group but he's obviously a world-class (unless you buy into the haunted-doll theory) ventriloquist who has also shown a lot of promise in the entertainment journalism industry, and Cat seems like the most genuineJack of All Tradesperformer- especially noted during her re-audition when she flawlessly performs a one-girl play scene, sings a show-tune and juggles in just 90 seconds. And if Trina realized that it was Martial Arts and her genuine physical ability rather thansinging and dancingthat was her special talent, she could find performing arts success through stunt work.

characters.name: Tori Vega
characters.description: The main character, Tori joins Hollywood Arts after filling in for her sister Trina during a performance. Tori quickly makes friends and enemies alike while attending the school. Tori's main talent is singing, but she can also act. Her best friends are André Harris and Cat Valentine. Whereas, her rival is Jade West. Alliterative Name: One of her posts onTheSlap.com states that if she had been a boy her parents would have named her Victor, so her nickname would have been Tor. This implies that her full name is Victoria Vega, and therefore fits this trope. Almost Kiss:A one-sided one with Andre inJade Gets Crushed.Another one withBeckin "Tori Goes Platinum", but she refusesout of respect for Jade's feelings. A one-sided one with Andre inJade Gets Crushed. Another one withBeckin "Tori Goes Platinum", but she refusesout of respect for Jade's feelings.

characters.name: André Harris
characters.description: Tori's best friend and a talented musician. Accidental Misnaming: Trina can never get his name right. This running gag trails off after the first few episodes. The Ace: Andre appears to be remarkably good at everything. Almost Kiss:Almost kisses Tori due to her posing as Jade in "Jade Gets Crushed". Aroused by Their Voice: Develops a crush on Jade after hearing her sing.

characters.name: Robbie Shapiro
characters.description: A part of the group with a crush on Cat and a puppet named Rex. Abhorrent Admirer: Towards Trina and later Cat in Episode 3. Subverted in Cat's New Boyfriend, when Trina seems to be warming up greatly towards him, and the show often hints that Cat and Robbie may like each other. Accidental Kiss: With Jade in "The Bad Roommate", tripping over a backpack. Acquired Situational Narcissism: During Robarazzi, he embarrasses his friends to gain internet fame, and says they're overreacting when they're upset. Luckily, this is the only instance of this from him, and his friends helped him see the error of his ways. All Jews Are Cheapskates: Is incredibly stingy with his money, to the point where he allows his phone to be essentially useless because he doesn't want to pay for phone service.

characters.name: Rex Powers
characters.description: Robbie's puppet, whom no one likes. Adapted Out: He is nowhere to be seen in one of theSam & Catspecials where Robbie appears but he doesn't, which is weird. Ambiguously Bi: InBeggin' On Your Kneeshe says Rider Daniels is hot, when everyone stares he merely replies "Stare all you want, I'm secure", which can be taken one of two ways, but even when a straight man compliments another man's looks he usually wouldn't use such a description. Then iniParty With Victoriousafter André yells at him, his response is to say he has beautiful skin as he (André) leaves. Ambiguously Sentient Object: The show makes it ambiguous if Rex is actually sentient or not. Robbie's friends act like he's real, though in an episode where Rex "dies", it's revealed they do so more or less to humor Robbie. However, in another episode surrounding Trina's harness being cut during a play, Rex is revealed to be the culprit, with Robbie having to cover it up — it's unclear if Rex actually sabotaged Trina's play of his own accord and ability, orif Robbie did it and was just shifting blame. In yet another episode, Rex is heard speaking while in Robbie's backpack, suggesting that he might actually be sentient after all. Breaking the Fourth Wall: Rex posts a worried question about the episode "Rex Dies" onTheSlap. Narrates in between commercial breaks during 'April Fools Blank'.

characters.name: Jade West
characters.description: A student at Hollywood Arts, who quickly makes enemies with Tori, due to her rubbing on Jade's boyfriend. Despite this, the two are often paired together and make a surprisingly good team. Her main talent is acting, but she can also direct and sing. She is dating Beck and is best friends with Cat. Aesop Amnesia: Sometimes. The most egregious example is after the episodeTori Goes Platinum. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: She's the school's dark-hairedAlpha Bitchwho's aloof and sassy on a good day. Alpha Bitch: Played with. The first episodes definitely portrays her as one, but later episodes show too many sides that an Alpha Bitch would not possess, the most telling of which being her circle of friends: she hangs out with Tori and company most of the time. That said, if the plot requires a Alpha Bitch-like antagonist, Jade is more than capable of stepping up to the challenge. Of course, as anyone who went to a performing arts or vocational high school can attest to, a gothAlpha BitchisTruth in Television. Always Second Best: She finds herself coming second to Tori rather often, and it boils her blood and is the basis of their rivalry. Most prominent in "Tori Gets Stuck".

characters.name: Cat Valentine
characters.description: A strange girl Tori meets at Hollywood Arts. She is best friends with Jade and Tori, along with being the object of Robbie's affections. Near the end of the show, her parents move to help take care of her insane brother, so she ends up moving in with her grandmother. She meets Sam at the timeSam & Catstarts and when her grandmother chooses to move into a retirement home, she and Sam become room-mates and they start a babysitting business together to help pay for their rent. Abandoned Catchphrase: Cat tends to yell "What's that supposed to mean?" whenever she misunderstood someone's comment. By the middle of season one, she has stop using this phrase. Addled Addict: She finds herself addicted to something in at least two episodes, to the point where they're the only things she can focus on most of the time. In "Robarazzi", it's shopping from theSky Store. In "Tori Goes Platinum", it's a children's candy called Bibble. Advertised Extra: Despite having a big role in theiParty with Victoriouscrossover, she has very few lines throughout due to suffering from vocal nodules, thus most of her dialogue came out of the speaker headband she wears. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!

characters.name: Beck Oliver
characters.description: Jade's boyfriend, whom Tori spilled coffee on during her first day. He is also arguably the most stable one out of the group. Almost Kiss:On Tori, but she refuses because she doesn't want to hurt Jade's feelings. Ambiguously Bi: Has a clear interest in girls but also once referred to a male costume designer as "adorable", though admittedly that might have just been to get a rise out of a jealous Jade. Ambiguously Brown: We just know that Beck is part Canadian. His actor Avan Jogia is a Canadian-born actor of Indian descent. Auto Erotica: Beck tried for this, but Jade wasn't in the mood. Probably for the best, seeing how there was a guy with a camera in the backseat.

characters.name: Trina Vega
characters.description: Tori's older sister, the residentButt-Monkeybecause of her annoying personality and her lack of talent. Trina is often self-centered, but genuinely loves her little sister. Abhorrent Admirer: Tries to flirt with Beck when he breaks up with Jade. He is not interested in her and, along with Andre and Robbie, teaches her after she spreads a rumor she's dating him in hopes other guys will ask her out. Action Girl: This seems to be what Trina actually does best, as she appears to make up in physical strength, agility and fighting skill, even when drugged up to the gills (Freak The Freak Out) what she lacks in singing ability. Her uniform, which was blue with a yellow belt, is actually a Vovinam Gi, not a Karate Gi. Also, unlike Karate, a yellow belt is the equivalent of a black belt;Trina Vega of all people is a highly skilled martial artist. A-Cup Angst:Impliedin "Tori the Zombie". While on the phone with a doctor, discussing Tori's problem, Trina asks if she needs her parents' permission to get minor cosmetic surgery. After hanging up, Trina laments that she can't get the surgery until she's eighteen, and glances down to her boobs momentarily. This would be ironic, considering how often the show comments about how busty she is. All of the Other Reindeer: She's friendless, hasn't amounted to anything, and is only popular among skeevy losers even more pathetic than she is.

characters.name: Sinjin van Cleef
characters.description: A weird student who helps out with technical stuff around the school. He also has a crush on Jade which borders on obsession. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: Apparently, 'he gives great crew' - he can operate lights/sound boards, and build props that are realistic enough to fool people (as he did for Tori inThe Great Ping-Pong Scam). IniParty With Victorious, he also proves to be extremely good at a surfing simulator (until it malfunctioned and threw him out the window). Butt-Monkey: He makes Robbie look like a winner in comparison. His status is lampshaded in "Tori Gets Stuck" where Jade complains about being cheated and humiliated. Sinjin tells her that it was something to get used to and Robbie nods in agreement. Casanova Wannabe: He tries unsuccessfully to flirt with all the girls. Cloud Cuckoolander: Where to start?

characters.name: Erwin Sikowitz
characters.description: The eccentric acting teacher at Hollywood Arts. He is the main mentor to the group, though he clearly has a greater attachment to Jade and Tori. Actually Pretty Funny: He unambiguously cares for his students, but he couldn't help but laugh as he watched Cat knock her classmates around in her desperation to use her phone in "Cell Block". Barefoot Loon: He's definitely on the zanier side, and noticeably avoids footwear. Brutal Honesty:Telling Jade "too bad" when she says she doesn't want to be Tori's Secret Santa in "A Christmas Tori." Earlier in the same episode, he even called Sinjin's sister a little weirdo right in his presence and outright told him his parents "should've stopped with him".In "Freak The Freak Out", when he tells Jade that she's lucky to have Beck as a boyfriend, and also slams Robbie for his lack of weekend plans.Played with in one episode, where he uses brutal honesty (disparaging Tori's singing and her chances of becoming a professional singer; however, he just says that to kit for reactions from the students) to demonstrate how playing against expectations in a way to draw the audience into an actor's performance. Telling Jade "too bad" when she says she doesn't want to be Tori's Secret Santa in "A Christmas Tori." Earlier in the same episode, he even called Sinjin's sister a little weirdo right in his presence and outright told him his parents "should've stopped with him".

characters.name: Burf
characters.description: Sinjin's best friend who made a handful of appearances in the third and fourth seasons. Black and Nerdy: He's a nerd who happens to have dark skin. Black Best Friend: He's Sinjin's best friend, and the only character seen hanging out with him on a consistent basis. Early-Bird Cameo: A few episodes prior to his first physical appearance, he appeared as part of the picture gallery for The Slap. '70s Hair: He has an afro that looks like it came straight out of the disco era.

characters.name: Lane Alexander
characters.description: The school's guidance counselor. He often acts as a secondary mentor to the group. Beware the Nice Ones: As seen inThe WoodandiParty With Victorious, though it may seem to be reasonable seeing his anger was triggered by Trina.The Wood, had him really go berserk on the TV crew. Demoted to Extra: Began showing up less in the later seasons. Meaningful Name: You could say thatLaneguides students down the rightroadssince he is the guidance counselor. Nice Guy: Most of the time.

characters.name: Festus
characters.description: The owner and runner of the Grub Truck, who sells food to the students of Hollywood Arts. The Alleged Car: So much so that Jade and Tori mistake it for a car they ordered from a junkyard inThe Wood. Funny Foreigner: He knows Spanish. Put on a Bus: After the special "Locked Up", Festus is never seen or mentioned again with no explanation as to why. Ruritania: Yerba, the country he comes from, as demonstrated inLocked Up!

characters.name: Ryder Daniels
characters.description: A student who regularly dates girls, uses them to get good grades, and then dumps them afterwards. He learns his lesson the hard way when he tries this on Tori. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He basically toyed with Tori's emotions just for a thrill and a decent grade. For the Evulz: He's a talented enough singer to have a gotten a good grade on his own and was clearly just messing with Tori's head to be an asshole. Intentional Heartbreaker: Dates girls, including Tori, solely for good grades, callously dumping them once they're no longer useful. He also toyed with Tori's emotions by temporarily breaking up with her and forcing her to win him back. Hate Sink: He's serial womanizer who has a bad habit of dating talented girls to get good grades, and dump them when he's done with them. He's done this to several girls, earning a bad rep at the school, and is smugly proud at breaking their hearts; at one point he feigns anxiety and temporarily breaks up with Tori to play with her emotions and get her to win him back.

characters.name: Helen Dubois
characters.description: Once the owner of a popular movie theater in San Diego, she becomes the new principal of Hollywood Arts in "Helen Back Again". Canon Immigrant: As she originated fromDrake & Joshand has now made her mark in theVictorioustimeline. Catchphrase: "That is not my job!" Charles Atlas Superpower:Tore the door off of someone's locker with easein assisting Trina in beating upRobbie who was posing as a mugger. Former Child Star: SaidCatchphraseactually made her famous.

characters.name: Vice Principal Dickers
characters.description: The vice principal of Hollywood Arts, who runs the detention the group finds themselves in ''The Breakfast Bunch". A Dick in Name:Dickers is not a very nice guy. Disproportionate Retribution: Gives Tori another week of detention because of Jade's snarky comment directed towards her, although it was more to do with the comment itself pissing him off. Expy: He is basically the Victorious version of Mr. Howard fromiCarly, as well as the respective spoof of Mr. Richard Dick Vernon, another counterpart fromthe movie this episode is based (up)on, as both areSadistic TeacherandChild Hater, who usually talk very loud and fast. Hair-Trigger Temper: A few snide comments from the gang is enough for him to give them a few more detentions.

characters.name: David And Holly Vega
characters.description: Adults Are Useless: In "Freak the Freak Out", after Trina got her wisdom teeth pulled out, they refuse to take care of her, instead they go to Santa Barbara and put Tori in charge. By the end, David walked in to see his daughter getting attacked by Hayley and Tara, heWALKS OUTof the house and tells his wife to get back in the car.He could have easily stopped thisby arresting or calling for backup as a police officer.He also cared more about the camera getting destroyed instead of his daughter Trina getting hurt by Tori. He also cared more about the camera getting destroyed instead of his daughter Trina getting hurt by Tori. Good Parents: Alternate between this and neglectful ones. Jerkass: They can be downright dismissive towards their children at times, with them being more cold to Trina and treating her more like an annoyance rather than a daughter. (Sure, Trina can be annoying, but still.) They slightly favor Tori more, but even then, they can be dismissive of her too. Mama Bear: Holly in "Crazy Ponnie".

characters.name: Charlotte Harris
characters.description: Cloudcuckoolander: More so thanCat. Conspiracy Theorist: Charlotte believes that the post office is "run by aliens trying to enter your home and steal your ketchup."What. The Cynic: An extreme version of this with herEverything Trying to Kill Youmindset. Everything Trying to Kill You: Believes this, amongst everything else. Funny Schizophrenia: It's implied, but never outright stated, that the explanation for her bizarre paranoid delusions is that she suffers from Schizophrenia. Due to its cartoonish portrayal, it sometimes slips intoDude, Not Funny!territory.

characters.name: Mr. West
characters.description: Defrosting Ice King: Jade described him as "cold and judgmental." He eventually admits that Jade's play was excellent. Jock Dad, Nerd Son: Hates everything concerning creative activities and believes that anyone who performs them are stupid. Lethal Chef: The one time he make breakfast for Jade, she spent the rest of the morning throwing up. Not Bad: He admits (with averted eyes) that he thought Jade's play was excellent. Parental Neglect: According to one of Jade's videos on the Slap, he never pays any real attention to her, constantly ignoring her in favor of his new wife.

characters.name: Cat's Brother
characters.description: Ax-Crazy: He got a few gallons of blood for Jade's play in "Prom Wrecker"... apparently, he missed the memo that it was supposed to befakeblood. Cloud Cuckoo Lander: He makes Cat look normal by comparison. The Ghost: For as often as we hear about him, we never see him. Made of Iron: He's been stabbed in Japan, shot by hisclown-dressed cousin, even fallen out of a 4th-story building onto the roof of a shuttle bus in Vegas... and he's still kicking. No Name Given: We never learn his name.Henry Dangerheavily implies that he's the social media star Frankini, but even then that's just his stage name.

characters.name: Hayley Ferguson and Tara Ganz
characters.description: Arc Villain: TheBig Bad Duumvirateof the "Freak The Freak Out" special. Beauty Is Bad: Their looks are hot, but their personalities are not. Seems to be a common flaw with girls that go to Northridge. Curb-Stomp Battle: On the receiving end andbrutallystomped upon by Cat and Jade during the karaoke contest. They get stomped again later in the episode by Tori. Daddy's Girl: Yet they both stood victorious in the end because Hayley's father was the owner of the club. Cat flat out implies that Hayley's father doesn't love her. It took another curb-stomping from Tori to have her father reconsider that decision. Evil Versus Evil: With Jade West.

characters.name: Hope Quincy
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Within thefirst minuteof her appearance, she happily invites Tori, Beck, and Robbie to sushi with her and Andre. By her second appearance, she's a full-blown bitch who questions Tori's presence at her party and outright tells her to keep her mouth shut. Clingy Jealous Girl: It's pretty clear later on that she is indeed jealous of Tori, most likely her friendship with Andre. Daddy's Girl: More so than Hayley, as it's visibly see how spoiled she is. It's subverted though, when she gains a minor concussion from falling debris during the earthquake, her father prefers to watch Tori's and Andre's performance for a second time than to meet her at the hospital. The party-goers actually did the same thing. Ding Dong The Witch Is Dead: The fact that she gets knocked out during the earthquake right in front of Andre puts a smile on his face. One-Shot Character: She only appears in one episode and is never seen or heard from ever again.

characters.name: Wing Lee
characters.description: Dragon Lady: Upon her makeover since opening Nozu's, though her actual ethnicity is unknown. Deal with the Devil: She was only going to invest in Jade's play if her daughter was to star as a singing angel. Unfortunately, her daughter was known as "talentless and irritating". Disposing of a Body: Outright told her employee to get rid of a stroke-feigning Trina in this manner.Wing: Just drag her body out by the dumpster and don't say nothing to nobody!Everyone:O_O Hoist by His Own Petard: Or something like that...a subverted example, it's implied that she caused the "mysterious fire" that burned down Wok Star to build Nozu. Played straight in her first appearance, in that her obsession with getting a picture with a celebrity for her wall made her miss opening night of the play. Insurance Fraud: It's implied this is what Mrs. Lee did to build her new restaurant Nozu; she claims Wok Star burned down in a "mysterious fire" with a not-so-convincing tone of voice when lamenting the incident, and explains she used the insurance money to build Nozu. It is very implied that construction of the new restaurant has left her cash-strapped, as she admits during an earthquake that she doesn't have insurance for Nozu.

characters.name: Dale Squires
characters.description: Asshole Victim: Right after hisJerkass Realization, he gets his ass kicked by Kendra on national television. Jerkass: Took all of the credit for the film Tori "directed" herself, and told her that's how the movie business is. Jerkass Realization: His conscious caught up with him and he gave Tori and the others the credit they deserved during his confession. Unfortunately, it was too late for that. Lazy Bum: Did completely nothing during the filming of the gang's movie and still took the credit for anything. Manipulative Editing: When he changed the credits in the movie.

characters.name: Kendra Harris
characters.description: Action Girl: Easily stopped the security guards while beating up Dale byslappingthem. Disproportionate Retribution: According to Robbie's picture of her on The Slap, she threw him out of a window for stepping on her toe. Green-Eyed Monster: There is a possibility that she is jealous of people with skinny figures due to her disdain for those who eat salads.Kendra: (Gives Tori an elevator-look) What do you eat? Salads?Tori: Sometimes.Kendra: Figures. No Good Deed Goes Unpunished: Inverted, and not in theLaser-Guided Karmasense; beating up Dale had gotten her an offer for her talk show according to The Slap. Sassy Black Woman: According to Robbie, she's someone you don't want to mess with.

characters.name: Kwakoo
characters.description: Ambiguously Brown: Despite how it seems, Kwakoo is not actually Japanese. However, he might be Polynesian, much like his actor. As Long as It Sounds Foreign: "Kwakoo" is not a real Japanese name, but in fact based on a Nigerian name "Kwaku". The Big Guy: He is Mrs. Lee's bodyguard at Nozu Stout Strength: While he is on the portly side, he's strong enough to hoist Tori over his shoulder, carry her a good distance, and then sit her down on a bar top, all with one arm.

characters.name: Melinda Murray
characters.description: And There Was Much Rejoicing: Everyone on the set rejoiced when Tori inadvertently had her sent to the hospital due to her arrow-injury. Alliterative Name:MelindaMurray Disproportionate Retribution: Fired Beck because he was friends with Tori, who had corrected her line while Beck had done nothing at all.Thenshe kicks Tori off the set. Hated by All: The whole castandcrewdespisedher. Impaled Palm: Melinda got a crossbow bolt through her palm, causing her to get pulled out of the film. Cue the staff and co-actors rejoicing over the cause of the accident and hailing"Crystal Waters"as a hero.

characters.name: Ponnie/Fawn Leibowitz
characters.description: Arson, Murder, and JaywalkingSikowitz: She's crazy! She stole things, had weird things in her backpack, and called everyone Debby.(At Ponnie) A real nut job, she is! Ascended Extra: Pretends to be one of the unnamed extras in Sikowitz' class:Ponnie:You probably never noticed me. I'm one of the quiet kids who sits in the back and just reacts to stuff.Tori:You're a "Shrugger"?Ponnie:(shrugs sheepishly and mumbles "Yeah.") Dark Action Girl: Apparently took out multiple trained police officers and divested one of his uniform. Despair Event Horizon: Was pushed to this due to social isolation. Eating Lunch Alone: Tori meets her for the first time in the bathroom stall.

characters.name: The Yerbanian Chancellor
characters.description: Arc Villain: He is the main antagonist ofLocked Up. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: He is heartbroken by the death of his pet octopus and has Tori's friends arrested for accidentally killing it. Eye Scream: One of his eyes stopped working after he was bitten by a vampire moth, and Tori's shoe flying off her foot and into his face blinds him in the other eye. Eyepatch of Power: Invoked. He wears an eyepatch due to his above mentionedEye Scream. After the mishap with Tori's shoe, he is now forced to wear two. Hair-Trigger Temper: He has the cast arrested for accidentally blinding his other eye and killing his octopus. He also refused to accept that Tori's apology unless she said shedeliberatelythrew her shoe at him.

characters.name: Mason Thornesmith
characters.description: Arc Villain: OfTori Goes Platinum. Expy: Seems to be one forGeorge Hawk.Mason is also a lot like Alan Krim, the central antagonist of the Drake & Josh finale "Really Big Shrimp". Both are aCorrupt Corporate Executivewho try to use the main character's talent for selfish ends, but while Alan wanted to tailor Drake's music to his own preferences without the musician's consent, Mason was more focused on sculpting Tori's image into something she wasn't. Mason also makes aHeel–Face Turn(sort of) and realizes image doesn't define talent, whereas Alan maintains his villainous convictions until he gets fired by his boss for his scheming. Mason is also a lot like Alan Krim, the central antagonist of the Drake & Josh finale "Really Big Shrimp". Both are aCorrupt Corporate Executivewho try to use the main character's talent for selfish ends, but while Alan wanted to tailor Drake's music to his own preferences without the musician's consent, Mason was more focused on sculpting Tori's image into something she wasn't. Mason also makes aHeel–Face Turn(sort of) and realizes image doesn't define talent, whereas Alan maintains his villainous convictions until he gets fired by his boss for his scheming. Jerkass: He doesn't care if he's ruining Tori's life and friendships. All he cares about is making her what he wants her to be. Kick the Dog: When Tori decides she isn't going to be his puppet, he doesn't take it very well.

characters.name: Mamaw Shapiro
characters.description: Expy: To Sylvia Fine fromThe Nanny(Also played byRenée Taylor).

characters.name: Oliver
characters.description: Descent into Addiction: At the end of "Tori Goes Platinum," Cat's roped him into relapsing. He makes Cat promise not to tell anyone. Recovered Addict: He used to have a big problem with eating bibble, then he cleaned up and decided to help others. It doesn't last. Scary Black Man: He has a default glare on his face and takes up a lot of space on screen. When Robbie offered Cat a little bibble, he punched the bag and shoved Robbie to the floor. He is stillvery compassionate to Cat, gently saying "no, baby, you can't" when she asks for some.
